reading.source: Aesop, Fables（《北风与太阳》，公有领域，改编）
reading.passage: The North Wind and the Sun were arguing about who was stronger. 'I am much stronger than you,' said the North Wind. 'Look at those travellers on the road. I can make them take off their coats.' The North Wind blew as hard as he could, but the travellers only pulled their coats more tightly around them. Then the Sun began to shine. The travellers felt warm, and soon they took off their coats. The Sun smiled and said, 'Gentleness works better than force.'

questions.q: What were the North Wind and the Sun arguing about?
Why did the travellers take off their coats at the end?
In the story, 'gentleness' means ___.
What does the story tell us?
options: Kindness can work better than force.
questions.answer: Kindness can work better than force.

reading.source: Aesop, Fables（《狐狸与葡萄》，公有领域，改编）
reading.passage: One hot afternoon, a hungry fox was walking through a garden. He saw some beautiful grapes hanging high on a vine. 'Those grapes look sweet and juicy,' he said. 'I must have them.' The fox jumped up again and again, but the grapes were too high for him. At last he was tired and his legs hurt. As he walked away, he said, 'I am sure those grapes are sour anyway. I do not want them.'

questions.q: What did the fox want?
Why did the fox say the grapes were sour?
In the story, 'sour' means ___.
What lesson can we learn from the story?
options: People sometimes pretend not to want what they cannot get.
questions.answer: People sometimes pretend not to want what they cannot get.
